profile.headline: Technology leader, mentor and contributor
profile.summary: First and foremost I am a problem solver. I have a technical background spreading over many years, but I’m well aware that technology is only an enabler to solve real-world problems and that those problems can only be properly addressed by truly understanding the underlying needs first. Business first, technology second.

positions.title: Managing Director
positions.description:
Agiloak is a specialist Healthcare Informatics Solution Provider dedicated to providing step change benefits to the public and private healthcare sector in a timely, efficient and cost effective manner through intelligent and appropriate solutions.

As founder of Agiloak in 2000 I've always been committed to providing a high-quality delivery focused service to our clients (Mid-Yorkshire Hospitals Trust, NHS Direct, CfH, BT, Roche, Sheffield Hallam University and others).

We recognise that every organization has its individual needs and we like to build a close partnership with our customers to ensure that those needs are met.

Let's Work Together.

honors.title: Terry Feest Award for Innovation
honors.description:
I received this award for work on the Renal Data Collaboration.

The UK Renal Registry (UKRR) recognise that many people contribute to the UKRR giving freely their own time and with very little direct recognition.  The ‘Terry Feest’ award was established in 2013 to acknowledge exceptional contributions.
honors.issuer: Issued by UK Renal Registry · Sep 2017

volunteerExperiences.description:
I became a trustee of the MPGN / DDD Support Group - a registered charity in the UK - in August 2016 because my son is a DDD patient and I felt I had a lot to offer the group.
My background in Healthcare IT and a scientific education (Chemistry with a research year in protein synthesis) means I can interpret much of the language of the clinicians and researchers into language that patients can more easily understand.
Using my extensive IT healthcare experience to help the Renal Registry in the building of the UKRDC data warehouse.
